1	# /wf:ship — interface declaration
2	
3	The machine-readable, externally-bindable surface of `ship`. A resolver reads
4	this file for the skill's declared slots and settings — **never** the SKILL.md
5	body. Everything in the body outside the declared slot markers is freely
6	rewordable implementation; the five sections below are the stable, contracted
7	surface (invocation shape, terminal block, slots + merge policies, settings
8	keys, safety rules).
9	
10	## Invocation
11	
12	`/wf:ship [<id>] [--status <name>]`
13	
14	## Terminal block
15	
16	`SHIP — <Merged | Blocked | Handed-off>`
17	
18	## Slots
19	
20	| slot (skill.point) | merge policy | purpose                                                                 |
21	|--------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
22	| ship.review        | replace      | the review-address step between green checks and the merge (Phase 4.5); the inline default drives no reviewer |
23	
24	## Settings
25	
26	_(none)_
27	
28	## Safety rules
29	
30	**Allowed:** read the task folder and its artifacts; obtain config via the
31	`wf-resolver` `resolve_config({ workspaceRoot, ... })` query; read-only resolution via
32	`workspace-root-resolve` and `current-branch-query`; resolve the `delivery`
33	surface once and invoke its **read** operations (`pr-detect`, `checks-read`) via
34	`resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` (`class: fragment`); resolve the `ship.review` slot via
35	`resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` (`class: slot`); invoke the sibling `wf:*` commands this skill
36	drives through the **Skill** tool (`/wf:branch`, `/wf:run` and each gated
37	`/wf:*` it names, `/wf:pr`, `/wf:tf`).
38	
39	**Forbidden:** write or edit any file (artifact, source, or config) — `ship` is
40	a dispatcher; finalize a merge while any delivery check is failing or unsettled
41	(never merge a red PR); run any destructive version-control operation or invoke
42	`pr-merge` directly (the single merge write is `/wf:tf`'s); improvise a review
43	step at the `ship.review` marker when the slot is unfilled or unresolved; name
44	any concrete tracker, delivery, or stack tool anywhere in this skill's
45	behaviour; write the model id, any AI-attribution trailer, a "generated with"
46	footer, an emoji, or any promotional tagline into any comment, commit, or output.

content.content: 1 --- 2 name: spec 3 description: Writes a grounded task specification (01_spec.md) for a task by fetching requirements from the active tracker capability (when registered), exploring the current codebase, and resolving ambiguities interactively. Use when the user starts a new task and needs to document scope before planning. 4 allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, Task] 5 --- 6 7 # /wf:spec — Grounded task specification from a task id 8 9 Write a spec (`01_spec.md`) for a task. Accepts a task id, fetches the work item through the active tracker capability (when one is registered) via direct provider resolution, creates a task folder under `{task-root}/`, and writes a grounded spec. Explores the codebase, resolves ambiguities interactively, and produces a clean spec. 10 11 --- 12 13 ## Prerequisites 14 15 Before the first bundled resolver MCP call in this skill/agent, run `pwd -P` and use the returned absolute current Agent/session workspace directory as `workspaceRoot` in every call. In a linked-worktree Agent, that cwd is the Agent's own worktree; never inherit a parent Agent's root. Pass `workspaceRoot` explicitly on every resolver call; omission is a hard schema error, and the resolver has no default or fallback root. 16 17 **Before any other phase**, obtain project config from the bundled `wf-resolver` MCP service via `resolve_config({ workspaceRoot, ... })` — it returns `{ workspaceRoot, registryPath, coreConfig{ taskRoot, … }, idShape }`, already resolved from `_local/config.md` (core performs no direct config-file parse). All references to `{task-root}` below come from `coreConfig.taskRoot` — never hardcode it. If the resolver reports the project is uninitialized (no resolved config / absent `_local/config.md`), stop and instruct the user to run `/wf:init` first. If the `wf-resolver` service is unavailable, stop and report that the resolver runtime is not loaded (restart Claude Code) — do not hand-parse config as a fallback. A registered tracker capability resolves its own project-scoped config (e.g. a tracker project name) from its own fragment binding; core never reads it directly. 18 19 --- 20 21 ## Command Syntax 22 23 ``` 24 /wf:spec [--type feat|fix|chore|refactor|migration|docs|hotfix] [--complexity S|M|L] 25 ``` 26 27 ### Arguments 28 29 | Argument | Required | Description | 30 | ----------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 31 | `` | NO | Task id — whatever shape the active tracker capability produces (opaque to core; e.g. a numeric or prefixed identifier), or a local `T` id when no tracker is registered. Falls back to inferring from the current branch. First run for a new task needs an explicit id (branch doesn't exist yet). | 32 | `--type ` | NO | One of: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `migration`, `docs`, `hotfix`. When supplied, wins over `/wf:classify` and is treated as confidence `high`. Defaults to whatever `/wf:classify` returns. | 33 | `--complexity `| NO | `S`, `M`, or `L`. Resolution order: `--complexity` flag → `triage.md` Size field → `M` default. | 34 35 ### Folder Convention 36 37 All task folders live under `{task-root}/` in the repo root: 38 39 ``` 40 {task-root}/{task-id}/ 41 ├── 00_reqs.md # Requirements (fetched from the active tracker, when registered) 42 ├── 01_spec.md # Specification (this skill) 43 ├── 02_plan.md # Implementation plan (wf:plan) 44 ├── research/ # Codebase exploration notes, analysis, investigations 45 ├── assets/ # Screenshots, mockups, trace files, images 46 └── artifacts/ # Diffs, test cases, test results, generated outputs 47 ``` 48 49 `{task-id}` is opaque: the active tracker capability's own shape when registered (e.g. a tracker-native identifier format), or the local `T` scheme otherwise. 50 51 **Core files** (`00_reqs.md`, `01_spec.md`, `02_plan.md`) live at the task folder root. 52 **Non-essential files** go into subfolders: 53 - `research/` — exploration notes, profiling results, investigation logs, architectural analysis 54 - `assets/` — images (screenshots, mockups, diagrams), trace files, binary files 55 - `artifacts/` — code diffs, test cases, test results, migration scripts, generated output 56 57 ### Validation 58 59 - **Resolve the tracker-surface state first** (direct provider resolution's scope-equality filter — "Direct provider resolution" below — applied at validation time, before any fetch): whether an active capability owns the `tracker` surface. 60 - **Tracker active:** `` must be supplied or inferable — a real tracker record needs a real id. If `` is provided, use it verbatim (opaque to core — whatever shape the active tracker capability produces). If omitted, infer a numeric token via `current-branch-query`, reached by resolving the `delivery` surface with the `wf-resolver` `resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "delivery" })` query (see "Direct provider resolution" below for the resolver-call pattern) and obtaining its body via the resolver's `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` content surface (`class: fragment`) and following it: extract the first 3+-digit run from the resolved branch name. **Resolve that token against `{task-root}`**: apply the same first-3+-digit-run extraction to each existing folder's name and compare it to the token (this matches both a tracker-prefixed shape like `-6396` and the local `T` scheme's own `T6396` uniformly). Exactly one match — reuse that folder's full name as `` verbatim; this recovers the opaque shape a prior invocation already established, core still never reconstructs it itself. Zero matches — the bare token isn't a deterministic `` — stop: "No task id provided and the branch-inferred token `` doesn't match an existing task folder. Pass the id explicitly: `/wf:spec `." More than one match — ambiguous — stop: "No task id provided and the branch-inferred token `` matches more than one task folder. Pass the id explicitly: `/wf:spec `." If no numeric token can be extracted from the branch at all, stop: "No task id provided and none could be inferred from the current branch. Pass the id explicitly: `/wf:spec `." 61 - **No tracker active (the contract's id-shape rule, local scheme):** if `` is explicitly provided, use it verbatim as `{task-id}`. Otherwise mint a fresh id: scan `{task-root}` for existing `T`-prefixed folders, take the highest, +1, zero-pad to 3 digits. **No stop condition** — an empty registry always yields a deterministic local id with no tracker call at all; there is nothing to infer and nothing to fail. 62 - **Task folder:** `{task-root}/{task-id}/`. Create if it doesn't exist. 63 - If `00_reqs.md` already exists in the folder, skip the tracker fetch and use the existing file. 64 - **Branch-name matching token.** Extract the first 3+-digit run from `` (whatever its shape) — call it `{numeric-id}`. This token is used **only** by the Phase 0.5 branch-gate quick-check (matching against an already-existing branch name); it plays no role in the task folder, the task id, or any tracker operation, all of which use the opaque ``/`{task-id}` form verbatim. 65 66 **Type resolution:** If `--type` is provided, use it (treat as `Confidence: high`). Otherwise, defer until Phase 0.7, which delegates to `/wf:classify`. Do NOT keyword-scan inline — the rubric lives in the classifier. 67 68 **Complexity resolution:** Apply in order, first match wins. 69 1. If `--complexity` is provided, use it. Source: `flag`. 70 2. Else, if `{task-root}/{task-id}/triage.md` exists and has a `**Size:** ` field (not `—`), use that value. Source: `triage`. 71 3. Else, default to `M`. Source: `default`. 72 73 Record the resolved value and source — both appear in the Final Output block so the user can see where the sizing came from. 74 75 --- 76 77 ## Phase 0: Create Requirements 78 79 Always runs first unless `00_reqs.md` already exists in the task folder. 80 81 ### Direct provider resolution (how `get`/`update` are reached) 82 83 Every tracker operation below (`get`, `update`) is reached by calling the bundled `wf-resolver` MCP tool `resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "tracker" })` — the typed query that returns the run-scoped resolution record `{ surface, owner, fragmentPath, state, degradation, diagnostics }` for the `tracker` surface. The resolver has already resolved the `## Capabilities` registry, the owning capability's `manifest.md`, and any plugin-anchored root (post install-manifest self-heal, per `capability-registry.ops.md` §"Recorded-root-first resolution with install-manifest self-heal"); core performs **no** registry / manifest / plugin-root read of its own. Obtain each op's body through the resolver's `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` content surface (`class: fragment`, keyed on the record's `owner` and fragment `ref`) and follow it in this skill's own context to dispatch `get`/`update` — never a raw `Read` of the path (the metadata queries return only paths/metadata; the body comes from `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })`). If the `wf-resolver` service is unavailable, stop and report that the resolver runtime is not loaded — do not hand-parse the registry as a fallback (WF-272 diagnostics/recovery). 84 85 Reproduce degradation from the record's `state`: 86 87 - **`ok`** — dispatch the operation against the resolved fragment. 88 - **`unconfigured`** (no capability owns `tracker`) — the silent local-only fallback: the `get` read proceeds silent local-only, no tracker operation attempted; every step below proceeds from local artifacts alone. 89 - **`unrecoverable`** (a registered capability's `tracker` manifest could not be read — recorded root dangled and the self-heal recovered nothing, named in the record's `diagnostics` string) — the `get` read stays silent local-only; the one tracker **write** (`update`, step 3 below) applies the residual diagnosis: a warn-once in the hedged candidate-naming form, reading the `diagnostics` string to name the candidate pack(s), per `capability-registry.ops.md` §"Recorded-root-first resolution with install-manifest self-heal" (Residual diagnosis). A genuinely `unconfigured` registry stays silent instead. 90 91 ### Fetch Procedure 92 93 1. **Fetch the work item and resolve parent context.** Invoke `get()` via direct provider resolution above. Its declared output — "the work item's current fields, state, and relations" — covers both the child fetch and the immediate parent's relation when present, even if the child description is complete. Parent items often contain scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, and cross-task constraints the child omits. 94 - **Unconfigured tracker** (the scope-equality filter matches zero rows), or a **registered-but-unrecoverable** tracker whose manifest couldn't be read — silent local-only fallback, no prompt, no error: continue to step 2 with no fetched data. The `get` read never emits the residual diagnosis; only the co-located `update` write does (step 3). 95 - **Configured and the fetch succeeds** — proceed with the fetched fields exactly as before. 96 - **Mid-run failure** (a tracker was registered but the `get` call errors) — warn once, naming the operation and the error, then continue local-only from whatever context is available. The run is never blocked by a tracker failure. 97 98 2. **Check for empty requirements.** If the child description is empty/minimal, use parent description as the primary requirement source. If both are empty/minimal, create a minimal requirements file and warn the user. 99 100 3. **Backfill an empty "Dev" child description (the library's single tracker write).** If ALL of the following hold: 101 - the child work item's title starts with `Dev` (e.g. `Dev`, `Dev:`, `Dev — backend part`), 102 - the child description is empty or minimal (blank, whitespace-only, or merely restating the title), 103 - a parent work item was resolved in step 1 and has a non-empty description, 104 105 then invoke `update(, description: )` via direct provider resolution: 106 - Compose `X` — the most concise statement of what's to be done, **5 words max**, derived from the parent title/description (e.g. `CSV export for audit log`). 107 - Pick the sentence by the parent's work item type: a bug-type parent → `Fix X as described in the parent bug ()`; any other type → `Implement X as described in the parent ()`. Core keys only on the generic bug/non-bug distinction — it never names a tracker-specific type taxonomy; a tracker capability that wants finer per-type wording contributes it through its own fragment. 108 - `` is an HTML anchor to the parent work item with link text `: ` (e.g. `6390: Audit log CSV export`), using whatever link the `get` output already supplies for the parent. If `get`'s output supplies no such link, omit the anchor and use the plain `: ` text instead. Description fields may carry the tracker's own markup — normalize to clean markdown when composing. 109 - Core names the field generically as `description` — never a tracker-specific field string; the active tracker capability's own fragment binds `description` to its concrete field. Never touch any other field, any other work item, or a non-empty description — this backfill is the only tracker write any skill in the library performs. 110 - Use the same sentence as the `## Description` body of `00_reqs.md` (step 6); the Parent Context section still carries the substance. 111 - **Registered-but-unrecoverable tracker** (a registered capability's manifest is unrecoverable — recorded root dangled and the self-heal recovered nothing — so zero readable `tracker` providers resolve): skip the backfill and **warn once** in the hedged candidate-naming form defined in `capability-registry.ops.md` §"Recorded-root-first resolution with install-manifest self-heal" (Residual diagnosis) — name the unreadable-manifest pack(s) from the `## Capabilities` row as candidates ("if one is your `tracker` provider, fix its stale root / re-run its init"), never asserting ownership — then continue local-only. This is the only message the tracker residual emits in this run: the co-located step 1 `get` stays silent, so the **net residual is exactly one warn-once, driven by this write**. A genuinely unconfigured registry (no readable-manifest pack is unrecoverable) stays silent instead. 112 - If `update` is unavailable (no tracker registered) or the write fails, continue the spec flow. When a tracker is registered but the write fails, record in `00_reqs.md`: "Child description backfill failed: ." 113 114 4. **Discussion comments and image attachments are a documented contract-completeness gap, not fetched.** The tracker provider surface has no `list_comments`/`get_attachments`-equivalent operation today — this is a known gap, tracked for a future tracker-contract extension, not a local workaround. Skip both; do not attempt an inline tracker-specific call to bridge the gap. 115 116 5. **Create the task folder** `{task-root}/{task-id}/` if it doesn't exist. 117 118 6. **Write `00_reqs.md`** in the task folder: 119 120 ```markdown 121 # {task-id}: {Work Item Title} 122 123 > Fetched from the active tracker (task #{id}) on {YYYY-MM-DD}, when a tracker capability is registered; otherwise a blank local requirements file. 124 > Type: {work item type} | State: {state} | Assigned: {assigned to} 125 > Fetched by: 126 > Discussion comments and image attachments are a documented contract-completeness gap — no `list_comments`/`get_attachments`-equivalent tracker operation exists today, so neither is fetched. Pending a future tracker-contract extension. 127 128 ## Description 129 130 {Work item description field — preserve original formatting, strip markup to clean markdown} 131 132 ## Acceptance Criteria 133 134 {Acceptance criteria field if present, otherwise omit this section} 135 136 ## Visual Context 137 138 {Summarize what task-related screenshots/diagrams show, when manually added under `assets/`. Include image file path(s) and concise observations. If no images exist, omit this section.} 139 140 ## Parent Context 141 142 {If a parent exists, include parent ID/title and the relevant constraints, acceptance criteria, and scope notes that affect this task. If no parent exists, omit.} 143 ``` 144 145 7. **Update the index.** Invoke `/wf:index {id} reqs ""` to record the requirements artifact. Pass the title verbatim from the fetched work item (truncate to 80 chars if longer; escape any `|` as `\|` so the index table doesn't break). 146 147 8. **Report** to the user, per the outcome of step 1: 148 - **Fetch succeeded:** "Fetched task {id} (+ parent context when present) -> `{task-root}/{task-id}/00_reqs.md`. Review before proceeding." If step 3 backfilled the child description, add: "Backfilled empty description from parent #." 149 - **No tracker registered:** "No tracker registered — created a local requirements file at `{task-root}/{task-id}/00_reqs.md`. Review before proceeding." 150 - **Mid-run tracker failure:** "Tracker fetch failed for task {id} (see the warning above) — continued local-only -> `{task-root}/{task-id}/00_reqs.md`. Review before proceeding." 151 152 9. **Continue** with the Branch Gate using the newly created `00_reqs.md`. 153 154 --- 155 ## Phase 0.5: Branch Gate 156 157 Before exploring the codebase or writing the spec, verify the current branch is correct for this task. Runs after Phase 0 so that `00_reqs.md` exists for `wf:branch` to derive a branch name. 158 159 1. **Resolve delivery-surface ownership first** — call `resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "delivery" })` on the `wf-resolver` MCP service (resolving the same `delivery` surface `wf:branch` acts on), before any branch read; the returned record carries `{ owner, fragmentPath, state, … }`. **`state: unconfigured` (bare-core mode)** — the branch gate is skipped entirely: no branch is resolved, `wf:branch` is not invoked, no error and no hard stop. Emit its compact metadata. If `status: stop` or `diagnostic` is non-null, stop and surface the routing diagnostic. Otherwise obey the returned `executionShape` per `invocation-runtime.ops.md` §"Resolver call root"; this evidence selects `isolated`, so invoke one **Task** with `subagent_type: wf:branch`, passing the task id `{id}` **and the forwarded `delivery` resolution record** resolved in step 1 (the optional spawn extension — `invocation-runtime.ops.md` §"Run-scoped provider forwarding"). Pass a non-null model selector and preserve inherited effort when null. (Do NOT call `/wf:branch` — that would load its SKILL.md into this skill's context. The subagent is self-sufficient.) 162 - On success (`BRANCH — created`/`switched`/`already-active`), inspect `Carry:`. `none`/`applied` continues directly to Phase 0.7. A preserved-entry/manual-follow-up carry stops here and surfaces that follow-up; the branch itself remains successful. 163 - On failure (`BRANCH — Error`), stop and surface the subagent's reason. 164 165 **Note:** when `{task-root}` is tracked, the branch operation automatically captures and reapplies the newly written `00_reqs.md`. Only a preserved-entry/manual-follow-up `Carry:` requires manual resolution before rerunning. 166 167 --- 168 169 ## Phase 0.7: Resolve Task Type 170 171 Determine the task's branch-type bucket (one of `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `refactor`, `migration`, `docs`, `hotfix`) before exploration so it can be persisted into the spec metadata. 172 173 1. **If `--type` was provided**, use that value. Set `Confidence: high` and `Alternative: —`. Skip the classifier call. 174 2. **Otherwise**, call `resolve_routing` immediately before dispatch with `workspaceRoot: `, `role: "classify"`, `unitIds: ["spec:classify"]`, `shapeEvidence: { workSurface: "external-context", atomicity: "atomic", unitCount: 1, unitsIndependent: false, ambiguity: "bounded", risk: "low", toolWork: "bounded", validation: "judgment", contextIsolation: "useful", independentReview: false, returnContract: "mechanically-judgeable", requestedParallelism: 1 }`, `supportsModelSelector: true`, and `supportsEffortSelector: false`. Emit its compact metadata. If `status: stop` or `diagnostic` is non-null, stop and surface the routing diagnostic. Otherwise obey the returned `executionShape` per `invocation-runtime.ops.md` §"Resolver call root"; this evidence selects `isolated`, so invoke one **Task** with `subagent_type: wf:classify`, passing `{id}` (resolved against the just-written `00_reqs.md`). Pass a non-null model selector and preserve inherited effort when null. Parse the `CLASSIFY — Complete` block for `Type`, `Confidence`, and `Alternative`. If the classifier returns `CLASSIFY — Error`, stop and surface the reason — do not guess a type inline. 175 3. **Branch on confidence:** 176 - `high` — use the type silently. `Alternative` is `—`. 177 - `medium` — use the primary type. Record the `Alternative` so it can appear in the spec metadata. 178 - `low` — raise an `AskUserQuestion` offering the primary and alternative types as options ("Pick the task type — classifier was uncertain"). Use the user's pick as the resolved type; the unpicked option becomes the Alternative. 179 4. Hold the resolved `(type, alternative)` pair in memory for Phase 3, where it is written into the spec metadata. 180 181 --- 182 183 ## Safety Rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE) 184 185 **Allowed:** 186 187 - Use sourcebot MCP tools (`mcp__sourcebot__search_code`, `mcp__sourcebot__read_file`, `mcp__sourcebot__list_tree`) for code search — preferred over raw `Grep`/`Glob` because it's indexed and cross-repo 188 - Read any file in the project (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) — fall back when sourcebot is unavailable or for file-pattern search 189 - Use MSSQL extension tools (`mssql_run_query`, `mssql_list_tables`, `mssql_list_views`, `mssql_list_schemas`) for database schema and data exploration 190 - Invoke `get`/`update` via the `wf-resolver` `resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "tracker" })` query — **read-only, with exactly one write exception**: Phase 0 step 3 may invoke `update` to patch the description field on the child work item, only when that description is empty/minimal, the title starts with `Dev`, and a parent with a real description exists. No other field or work item may ever be written. 191 - Read-only resolution via `current-branch-query` (the `wf-resolver` `resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "delivery" })` query) 192 - Write/create files ONLY inside the task folder (`{task-root}/{task-id}/`) 193 - Invoke the **Task** tool with `subagent_type: wf:branch` for the Phase 0.5 branch gate. The wf:branch subagent performs only non-destructive delivery actions — creating or switching to the task branch, fetching the base, and publishing the branch upstream; it never resets, force-pushes, deletes branches, or commits. Invoke the **Task** tool with `subagent_type: wf:classify` for Phase 0.7 type resolution (read-only). 194 195 **Forbidden:** 196 197 - Modify any source file outside the task folder 198 - Run builds, tests, linters, or installs 199 - Run any destructive version-control operation directly (the delegated wf:branch subagent is constrained to non-destructive ops above) 200 - Create implementation plans or step-by-step checklists (that is `/wf:plan`'s job) 201 202 --- 203 204 ## Phase 1: Explore the Codebase 205 206 Before writing the spec, explore the project to understand the current state. This grounds the spec in reality rather than assumptions. 207 208 1. **Read `00_reqs.md`** from the task folder to understand the requirements. Identify relevant areas of the codebase. Review the `Visual Context` notes and any images in `assets/` (mockups, diagrams, screenshots) before searching code. 209 210 2. **Search the codebase** — try sourcebot MCP first (`mcp__sourcebot__search_code`); fall back to Glob/Grep if sourcebot is unavailable or for file-pattern searches. Find: 211 - Files that implement related functionality 212 - Existing patterns, conventions, and architectural decisions 213 - Tech stack details (frameworks, languages, key dependencies) 214 215 3. **Explore database schema** using MSSQL extension tools (`mssql_list_tables`, `mssql_list_views`, `mssql_run_query`) if the task involves data models, persistence, or queries. 216 4. **Read key files** to understand the current implementation state. 217 5. **Note constraints** — discover any technical constraints, existing APIs, data models, or conventions that the spec must account for. 218 6. **Identify boundaries** — find what changes would be safe (low-risk, well-tested areas) vs. risky (shared modules, public APIs, database schemas). 219 7. **Save exploration notes** to `research/exploration.md` if the exploration is extensive (L complexity). For S/M, inline findings into the spec's Context section. 220 221 The goal is context, not a plan. Collect facts that inform WHAT to build, not HOW. 222 223 --- 224 225 ## Phase 2: Resolve Open Questions 226 227 After exploration, identify any ambiguities or decisions that affect the spec. Resolve them NOW so the spec ships clean. 228 229 1. **Identify questions** — ambiguities in the description, technical decisions with multiple valid approaches, unclear scope boundaries, constraints that need confirmation. 230 2. **Prompt the user** — use `AskUserQuestion` with suggested options derived from exploration. Offer concrete choices, not open-ended questions. 231 3. **Record resolutions** — bake answers into the spec as confident statements. No residual Q&A in the output. 232 233 If no questions exist, skip to Phase 3. 234 235 --- 236 237 ## Phase 3: Write the Spec 238 239 Write `01_spec.md` in the task folder using the template below. 240 241 **Overwrite if `01_spec.md` exists** (version-control history preserves prior versions). 242 243 **Writing principles:** 244 245 - **Machine-verifiable success criteria.** Not "the feature works" but "POST /api/auth/login returns 200 with JWT when given correct credentials." 246 - **Explicit scope boundaries.** State what is IN and what is OUT. 247 - **Constraint-based framing.** State constraints alongside the objective, not separately. 248 - **Reference code, don't describe it.** Point to existing files as examples of patterns to follow. 249 - **Spec sizing by complexity:** 250 - `S` — 100-200 words 251 - `M` — 300-500 words 252 - `L` — 500-1000 words 253 - **Focus on What & Why.** Leave the How to `/wf:plan`. 254 - **Clean of Q&A.** Resolved questions become confident statements. 255 256 --- 257 258 ## Spec Template 259 260 The verbatim `01_spec.md` template — the metadata block, `## Objective`, `## Success Criteria`, `## Context`, `## Scope`, `## Constraints`, `## User Journeys`, and `## Boundaries` — lives at `spec-template.md`, obtained via the resolver's `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` (`class: references-template`, `skill: spec`, `ref: spec-template.md`), never a raw `Read` of the plugin-cache path. It is read only on this write path (Phase 3), so it stays out of the boot body. Follow it, then emit it with placeholders substituted. 261 262 Sections are optional — omit any that would be empty. Only include an "Open Questions" section if some questions are truly unresolvable (e.g., depends on an external team decision). 263 264 **After writing the spec**, invoke `/wf:index {id} spec " · · success criteria"` to record it in the per-task index. Substitute the resolved values (e.g. `feat · M · 4 success criteria`). 265 --- 266 267 ## Edge Cases 268 269 - **Tracker fetch outcome (configured / unconfigured / failed):** **Unconfigured** (no active tracker-surface owner) — silent local-only fallback, no prompt, no error; proceed with a blank local requirements file. **Configured and the fetch succeeds** — proceed with the fetched fields exactly as before. **Configured but the `get` call fails mid-run** — warn once, naming the operation and the error, then continue building `00_reqs.md`/`01_spec.md` from whatever local/partial context is available. The run is never blocked by a tracker failure. 270 - **Fetched work item has empty description:** Use parent work item when available. If the child title starts with `Dev`, also backfill via `update` per Phase 0 step 3. If parent also empty, create minimal `00_reqs.md` with title only, skip the backfill, and warn user. 271 - **No tracker registered:** Not fatal, not a failure — the silent local-only fallback. Continue the spec; do not record a failure note (there is nothing to have attempted). 272 - **Tracker registered but the backfill write fails (permissions, etc.):** Not fatal. Continue the spec; record the failure reason in `00_reqs.md`. 273 - **Registered-but-unrecoverable tracker (recorded root dangled, self-heal recovered nothing):** When the install-manifest self-heal recovers the root, resolution heals in-memory and the `get`/`update` just work — no re-init, no error. When it stays unrecoverable, the Phase 0 `get` read is silent local-only (no message) and the `update` backfill warns once in the hedged candidate-naming form — naming the unreadable-manifest pack(s) from the `## Capabilities` row as candidates ("if one is your `tracker` provider, fix its stale root / re-run its init"), never asserting ownership — for a net of exactly one warn-once driven by the write. Distinct from a genuinely unconfigured registry, which stays silent. 274 - **Complexity is L:** Add a note in the spec: "Consider breaking this into sub-specs before planning." 275 - **Folder already has `01_spec.md`:** Overwrite it. 276 - **Folder already has `02_plan.md`:** Warn: "A plan already exists. The spec will be updated but the existing plan may be outdated." 277 - **No project files found:** Ask the user for the project root path to explore. 278 - **All questions resolved:** Omit the "Open Questions" section entirely. 279 280 --- 281 282 ## Final Output 283 284 ``` 285 SPEC — Complete 286 287 Task: {task-id} — 288 Type: <feat | fix | chore | refactor | migration | docs | hotfix> (source: <flag | classify-high | classify-medium | classify-low-user-confirmed>) 289 Complexity: <S | M | L> (source: <flag | triage | default>) 290 Folder: {task-root}/{task-id}/ 291 Spec: {task-root}/{task-id}/01_spec.md 292 Next: /wf:plan {id} 293 ``` 294 295 **The final output block must always be the very last thing output to chat.** 296

120	1. **Open it.** Route this edge with `workspaceRoot: <absolute pwd -P workspace root>`, `role: "pr"` and `unitIds: ["ship:pr"]` under §"Fixed sibling-Skill routing", then invoke `/wf:pr <id>` through the Skill tool — it commits and pushes any pending work and opens the pull request through the delivery provider. Read its `PR —` block; on its error state → `SHIP — Blocked`, surface the reason, stop.
121	
122	2. **Confirm it exists.** Invoke the delivery `pr-detect` operation (obtain its body via `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` from the Phase-1 record and follow it) for the task branch. If no open pull request is found → `SHIP — Blocked` ("`/wf:pr` opened no pull request for the task branch"), stop — never fabricate one. Otherwise capture the pull request reference for the phases below.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## Phase 4: Wait for the delivery checks to settle
127	
128	Never merge a red or unsettled pull request. Invoke the delivery `checks-read` operation for the pull request (obtain its body via `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` from the Phase-1 record and follow it) and evaluate the returned check states:
129	
130	- **No checks configured** (an empty check set) → vacuously settled and green; proceed.
131	- **All checks passing** → settled and green; proceed.
132	- **Any check failing** → **`SHIP — Blocked`**, naming the failing check(s). No merge — a red pull request is never merged. Stop.
133	- **Any check still pending / in progress** → re-read `checks-read`, **capped** at a small number of attempts. If every check has resolved to passing within the cap, proceed. If any resolves to failing → the failing-check stop above. If checks are still pending after the cap → **`SHIP — Blocked`** ("delivery checks did not settle within the cap"). No merge. Stop.
134	
135	The cap keeps the wait bounded so an unattended run can never hang indefinitely; a genuinely slow pipeline is reported honestly and re-run, never merged early.
136	
137	## Phase 4.5: Review attachment point (the `ship.review` slot)
138	
139	This is the declared `ship.review` composition point — between green checks and the merge — where a review-address step attaches (declared in `skills/ship/interface.md`, merge policy `replace`). Resolve it lazily with **one** call: `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` with `class: slot`, `skill: ship`, `point: review`. Act on the typed outcome — never improvise a review step at this marker:
140	
141	- **`{status: unfilled}`** (no slot contribution registered and no personal `_local/slots/ship.review.md` override — the state whenever no review capability is registered) → execute **exactly** the inline-default region below, then proceed to Phase 5. No reviewer is driven and no review finding is addressed — the checks-green state from Phase 4 carries into the merge unchanged.
142	- **`{status: composed, content, policy, …}`** → a fill is registered; **follow the served `content` as prose** in this skill's own context (a `replace` fill supersedes the inline default wholesale), then proceed to Phase 5.
143	- **`{status: unresolved}`** (registry-invalid / ref-not-found) or **`{status: refused}`** → do not improvise: run the inline-default region below (proceed to Phase 5) and state the resolver's reason. Follow the content surface's degradation discipline — never a wrong-path body, never a raw-read fall-through.
144	
145	<!-- wf:slot ship.review -->
146	No review step runs here. `ship` drives build → checks → merge only: at this point it addresses no review findings and drives no reviewer. Proceed to Phase 5 with the Phase-4 checks-green state unchanged.
147	<!-- wf:slot-end ship.review -->
148	
149	---
150	
151	## Phase 5: Merge and finalize
152	
153	**[ceiling checkpoint]** Before finalizing, apply the context-ceiling checkpoint (§"Context ceiling checkpoint"). This is the safest hand-off boundary: the branch is pushed and the PR is open, so the entire durable state survives. A fresh `/wf:ship <id>` re-detects the open PR, re-reads the settled checks, and merges — no work is repeated and nothing is stranded.
154	
155	Route this edge with `workspaceRoot: <absolute pwd -P workspace root>`, `role: "finalize"` and `unitIds: ["ship:finalize"]` under §"Fixed sibling-Skill routing", then invoke `/wf:tf <id>` (forwarding `--status <name>` when passed) through the Skill tool. The finalizer merges the pull request through the delivery provider's `pr-merge` operation (detect-first — never a double-merge), posts the resolution comment and closes the work item through the tracker provider when one is registered, then archives the task folder and updates the index locally. Read its `TF —` block:
156	
157	- `TF — finalized` (merged, or already merged) → **`SHIP — Merged`**, naming the merged pull request.
158	- `TF — partial` (a configured provider step failed mid-run — merge blocked by checks/conflicts, or a tracker error) → **`SHIP — Blocked`**, surface `/wf:tf`'s stated reason; the merge can be retried by re-running once the blocker clears.
159	- `TF — already-finalized` → the task was already merged and archived → **`SHIP — Merged`** (idempotent no-op).

1	# ship.review — the pre-merge review gate (slot fill)
2	
3	
4	Before following any resolver MCP call in this document, run `pwd -P` and use the returned absolute current Agent/session workspace directory as `workspaceRoot`. In a linked-worktree Agent, that cwd is the Agent's own worktree; never inherit a parent root. Pass it explicitly on every call. Omitting `workspaceRoot` is a hard schema error; resolver MCP calls have no default or fallback root.
5	The `pr-review` capability's fill for the `ship.review` slot (`replace` policy). `ship`
6	reaches this point **after** Phase 4 has confirmed the delivery checks green and **before**
7	Phase 5 merges. Because this is a `replace` fill it **supersedes** `ship`'s inline default
8	(the no-op "drive no reviewer") wholesale, and `ship` follows this prose in its own context.
9	
10	**Role framing.** This gate never mutates source and never merges. Its only outputs are
11	(a) replies posted on review threads and (b) a single **pass** or **block** decision. On any
12	block it emits `SHIP — Blocked` (with a `Reason:` and a `Next:`) and **stops** — it does not
13	fall through to Phase 5. On a pass it returns quietly and `ship` proceeds to Phase 5.
14	`ship`'s never-merge-red invariant and `/wf:tf`'s detect-first `pr-merge` stay the final guard.
15	
16	**Conservative by construction.** Any state that is not *provably clean* or *provably
17	addressed* blocks. "Unknown" is never treated as "clean". A "no review" claim is only ever
18	made after an API read-back at HEAD_SHA was actually performed.
19	
20	**Host access.** Every read/write below is a `delivery`-surface operation. `ship` already
21	resolved the `delivery` provider (its Phase 1 record); obtain each operation's body via
22	`resolve_content` (`workspaceRoot`, `class: fragment`) from that record and follow it in-context — name no
23	concrete host tool here. The operations this gate uses: `review-threads-read` (HEAD_SHA-scoped
24	finding-thread read), `pr-comments-read` (review-summary presence + reviewed-file signal), and
25	`review-thread-reply` (per-thread reply keyed by the thread node id). Verifying a finding
26	against the real code uses `Read` / `Bash` (grep) only.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Step 1 — Read back the review at HEAD_SHA (never assume "no review")
31	
32	Invoke `review-threads-read` for the PR branch. It returns `<read-performed>` (bool) and
33	`<threads>` (each: thread node id, anchor path + line, resolved/unresolved, body).
34	
35	- **`<read-performed> = false`** → the HEAD_SHA read-back did **not** happen (no branch/PR
36	  context, or a bare-core/degraded delivery provider). The review state is **unknown**.
37	  **Block:** reason `review read-back at HEAD_SHA could not be performed — review state
38	  unknown, not clean`. **Never** report "no review landed" — that claim requires a performed
39	  read-back. Stop. *(WF-313 req 1.)*
40	- **`<read-performed> = true`** → a real read against HEAD_SHA occurred (its thread set may be
41	  empty). Continue. Split on `<threads>`:
42	  - **One or more unresolved finding threads at HEAD_SHA** → Step 3.
43	  - **No unresolved finding threads at HEAD_SHA** → Step 2.
44	
45	Resolved threads at HEAD_SHA are already **fixed in code** (the finding was accepted and the
46	thread resolved) — they need no new reply and never block.
47	
48	## Step 2 — Zero unresolved threads: reviewed-clean vs zero-files vs not-yet-reviewed
49	
50	A performed read-back with no unresolved threads is ambiguous — it can mean "reviewed, no
51	findings", "the reviewer could not review any files", or "no review has posted yet". Resolve
52	it with `pr-comments-read`, whose reviews carry each reviewer summary and the commit it was
53	made against:
54	
55	- **A review is present at HEAD_SHA and it reviewed files** (its summary does not indicate a
56	  zero-file outcome) → genuinely reviewed, no findings → **clean pass** → Step 4.
57	- **A review is present at HEAD_SHA but reviewed zero files** — cause-agnostic: a "wasn't able
58	  to review any files" summary, an empty reviewed-file set, a diff-size skip, or any other
59	  cause → the review **did not happen**. This is the distinct **zero-files-reviewed failure**,
60	  never reported as "no findings". **Block:** reason `review resolved zero files at HEAD_SHA
61	  (zero-files-reviewed failure) — the review did not happen; not "no findings"`. Stop.
62	  *(WF-313 req 3.)*
63	- **No review present at HEAD_SHA:**
64	  - **a reviewer was requested** (a review is assigned/requested on the PR) but none has
65	    posted → it has not landed yet. Re-read `review-threads-read` + `pr-comments-read`,
66	    **capped** at a small number of attempts (2). If a review appears within the cap → resume
67	    this step's classification. If the cap is hit with still no review at HEAD_SHA → the poll
68	    **timed out**; the state is **unknown**, never clean. **Block:** reason `review requested
69	    but did not land within the capped polls — state unknown, not clean`. Stop. *(WF-313 req
70	    2 — a timeout is unknown, never clean.)*
71	  - **no reviewer was ever requested** on this PR → there is genuinely no reviewer in play and
72	    the read-back was performed and found none. This is an honest **reviewer-absent pass** (it
73	    is not a "no review landed while findings existed" claim — the read-back happened and the
74	    thread set is truly empty) → Step 4.
75	
76	## Step 3 — Every finding thread gets a reply before merge; fixed-in-code vs thread-answered
77	
78	For **each unresolved finding thread** at HEAD_SHA, verify it against the actual code at its
79	anchor — open the anchored `path`:`line` with `Read` / `Bash` (grep) and decide for yourself.
80	A review comment is a **hypothesis, never truth**. Then post **exactly one** reply via
81	`review-thread-reply(<thread-id>, <body>)`, recording its resolution class as the reply body's
82	first line so the two are distinguishable in the audit trail *(WF-313 req 5)*:
83	
84	- **Fixed in code** — the code at HEAD_SHA already satisfies the finding (the diff addressed
85	  it). Reply body begins `Resolution: fixed in code — ` then a one-line note of what in the
86	  code satisfies it. Thread **cleared**.
87	- **Thread answered (false positive)** — reading the code shows the finding does not hold
88	  (reviewer misread, style-only, the line moved). Reply body begins `Resolution: thread
89	  answered — ` then the one-line evidence from the code. Thread **cleared for merge** (it is
90	  answered, not silent); leave it open for reviewer adjudication and flag it in the report.
91	- **Thread answered (confirmed unaddressed)** — the code at HEAD_SHA does **not** satisfy the
92	  finding and it is a genuine defect this gate cannot fix (it mutates no source). Reply body
93	  begins `Resolution: thread answered — ` then `confirmed unaddressed; blocking merge`. Thread
94	  **not cleared**.
95	
96	Post a reply on **every** unresolved thread **before** deciding — even when the outcome is a
97	block — so no finding is ever left silent (the silent-finding failure this gate exists to
98	prevent) *(WF-313 req 4)*. Then:
99	
100	- **Any thread is "confirmed unaddressed"** → **Block:** reason `<n> confirmed finding(s)
101	  unaddressed at HEAD_SHA — run /wf-review:address-pr, then re-ship`. Stop.
102	- **Every thread cleared** (fixed-in-code or answered-false-positive) → Step 4.
103	
104	## Step 4 — Pass
105	
106	The review state is provably one of: reviewed-clean, reviewer-absent with a performed
107	read-back, or every finding thread cleared with a recorded reply. Return quietly so `ship`
108	proceeds to Phase 5. Carry a one-line gate summary into `ship`'s final block (e.g.
109	`Review: clean at HEAD_SHA` / `Review: 3 threads — 2 fixed in code, 1 answered`).
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Outcome → `ship` mapping
114	
115	| Gate outcome | `ship` action |
116	|--------------|---------------|
117	| unknown (no read-back / poll timeout) | `SHIP — Blocked` — stop before merge |
118	| zero-files-reviewed failure | `SHIP — Blocked` — stop before merge |
119	| confirmed unaddressed finding(s) | reply on every thread, then `SHIP — Blocked` — stop |
120	| reviewed-clean / reviewer-absent (read-back performed) | pass → Phase 5 |
121	| every finding thread cleared + replied | pass → Phase 5 |
122	
123	Rationale, the incident this gate answers, and the per-requirement mapping:
124	[`../references/ship-review.md`](../references/ship-review.md) — read by authors, never at
125	slot-fire.
126

1	# linear tracker provider — runtime ops
2	
3	**Version:** 1.4.0 (WF-213 — split out of the tracker fragment as the bounded runtime-ops half; mirrors the delivery split proven in WF-211; WF-158 — three read-only query operations bound: `list_by_status`, `list_milestones`, `list_cycles`; WF-282 — `resolve_config` distinguishes the relocatable capability registry from the fixed `_local/config.md` provider config; WF-300 — `resolve_config` reads the `## Linear` section from `_local/config.md` unconditionally, never from a relocated `registryPath`: provider config is not the capability registry; WF-315 — `list_blockers` bound to Linear's `blockedBy` relation)
4	**Role:** the runtime-read half of the linear tracker provider — every input, guard, MCP tool binding, and outcome mapping a tracker operation follows. Read at every tracker-surface boot; self-sufficient (no step below requires opening another file).
5	**Reference (grounding legend, per-operation grounding status, scope framing, coverage table — never read at boot):** `tracker.md`.
6	**Resolved by:** `plugins/wf/skills/_contracts/invocation-runtime.ops.md` §"Direct provider resolution" — a core skill selects the registry row where `contribution-kind = provider AND scope = tracker`, reads this file, and follows it in-context. No subagent, no phase gate.
7	**Model:** claude-opus-4-8
8	
9	**Consumes, never derives:** every operation takes an already-resolved id / title / body / field value; composing those from a tracker record (branch name, commit subject, …) is the caller's job, not this file's. The no-provider local `T<NNN>` fallback is core's own behaviour for the unconfigured surface (`capability-registry.ops.md` §"The tracker provider surface") — this file does not implement it.
10	
11	**Id shape:** `create_umbrella` / `create_child` return whatever identifier Linear's own `save_issue` response carries — `<LETTERS>-<NUMBER>` (e.g. `WF-136`). There is no local prefix to compose; Linear mints the whole identifier itself.
12	
13	**Configuration.** Read the `## Linear` section of `_local/config.md` (written by `/wf-linear:init`):
14	
15	- **Linear Team** — the team new issues are created under. Required for every write operation below; unset (still the `<...>` bracket placeholder, or the section missing entirely) means **unconfigured** — see `resolve_config`.
16	- **Linear Project** — optional secondary scoping. The literal value `none` (no brackets) means "do not scope created issues to a project"; any other non-bracketed value is a project name to resolve.
17	
18	**Team/project id resolution (shared by every write and query below).** `save_issue`, the status/label lookups, and the query operations all need Linear's internal `teamId` (and, when configured, `projectId`), not the human-readable name in config. Resolve once per run and reuse:
19	
20	1. `teamId` — call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_teams`, match the configured **Linear Team** value against each team's key or name, take the matching team's id.
21	2. `projectId` — only when **Linear Project** is not the literal `none`: call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_projects`, match the configured value against a project's name (scoped to the resolved team, when the tool supports narrowing), take the matching project's id.
22	
23	Cache both within the run; **do not re-resolve per call**.
24	
25	**Reducible probe list (spec pin):** none beyond what is already consolidated here. Team/project id resolution above is already **resolve-once-per-run-and-cache** — the single probe consolidation this fragment carries. `set_status`'s status-id lookup is deliberately **per-call and uncached** (workflow states differ by team; a cached id is not portable) and must not be reduced. Every other operation is a single MCP call. All per-operation call counts are unchanged by this split.
26	
27	**Operations:** resolve_config · create_umbrella · create_child · update · get · list_children · post_comment · set_status · attach_link · list_by_status · list_milestones · list_cycles · list_blockers.
28	
29	## resolve_config
30	
31	**Inputs:** none.
32	
33	**Procedure:**
34	
35	1. Read the `## Linear` section of `_local/config.md` — the fixed conventional location `/wf-linear:init` always writes provider config to. This is **independent of `registryPath`**: a project's `wf.config.js` may relocate the capability **registry** (the `## Capabilities` table) via `registryPath`, but core and provider config always stay in `_local/config.md`. The resolver models exactly this split — it reads core/provider config from `_local/config.md` unconditionally and honors a relocated `registryPath` only for the registry table — so the `## Linear` section is **never** anchored to the resolver-supplied `registryPath`; do not read it there.
36	2. **Configured** — the **Linear Team** row holds a real value: not the `<...>` bracket placeholder `/wf-linear:init`'s template uses for an unset value, and not a missing section/file.
37	3. **Unconfigured** — **Linear Team** is still a placeholder, or the section/file is missing entirely. This is the silent local-only fallback the contract's degradation rules define — **no prompt, no error**. (**Linear Project**'s state never gates configured/unconfigured — it is a secondary scoping value, defaulted to the literal `none` when unset.)
38	4. No `wf-resolver` call is needed to locate this section — its location is a fixed convention, not a resolver-supplied fact. The Linear config-section values themselves aren't yet a resolver-supplied fact either (the snapshot's `providerConfig` field is populated by the owning provider surface itself, per WF-270, and isn't wired through any typed tool response today), so reading them stays a direct local read of `_local/config.md`.
39	
40	**Output:** `configured` or `unconfigured`.
41	
42	## create_umbrella
43	
44	**Inputs:** task title, task description.
45	
46	**Procedure:**
47	
48	1. Resolve `teamId` (and `projectId`, if **Linear Project** is configured) per "Team/project id resolution" above.
49	2. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue` with `title`, `teamId`, `projectId` (if resolved), `description`. No `parentId` — this is the top-level issue.
50	
51	**Idempotency guard:** the returned id is recorded as a `**<label>:** <value>` metadata line in the local artifact that triggered the call. Before invoking `create_umbrella` again for the same artifact/slot, read that line back first; a present value means the umbrella already exists — **never** re-invoke for that artifact.
52	
53	**Output:** the created issue's identifier (`<LETTERS>-<NUMBER>`, e.g. `WF-136`).
54	
55	## create_child
56	
57	**Inputs:** parent issue id, child title, child description.
58	
59	**Procedure:**
60	
61	1. Resolve `teamId` the same way as `create_umbrella` (a child issue inherits the configured team unless the caller supplies a different one explicitly).
62	2. Call `save_issue` with `title`, `teamId`, `parentId: <parent-issue-id>`, `description`. Used both for a task's own child issues and for further nesting beneath those.
63	
64	**Idempotency guard:** identical to `create_umbrella` — the returned child id is recorded as a metadata line in the triggering local artifact; read it back before ever re-invoking `create_child` for the same artifact/slot.
65	
66	**Output:** the created child issue's identifier.
67	
68	## update
69	
70	**Inputs:** issue id, one or more fields to patch.
71	
72	**Procedure:**
73	
74	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue` with `id: <issue-id>` and only the changed field(s) (title/description/labels/estimate/etc.). `save_issue` is the single create-or-update primitive: passing an `id` selects the update path, omitting it (per `create_umbrella` / `create_child`) selects create.
75	
76	**Unrestricted binding:** `update` accepts whatever field(s) the caller supplies — `save_issue` is general-purpose; this fragment does not narrow it to any particular field.
77	
78	**Output:** confirmation the patch applied (or the tool's error, surfaced by the caller per the contract's mid-run-failure degradation rule).
79	
80	## get
81	
82	**Inputs:** issue id.
83	
84	**Procedure:**
85	
86	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue` with `id: <issue-id>`.
87	
88	**Output:** the issue's current title, description, status, parent, and labels.
89	
90	## list_children
91	
92	**Inputs:** parent issue id.
93	
94	**Procedure:**
95	
96	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues` filtered to `parentId: <parent-issue-id>`.
97	
98	**Output:** the parent's existing child issues (id + title, at minimum).
99	
100	## post_comment
101	
102	**Inputs:** issue id, comment body.
103	
104	**Procedure:**
105	
106	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_comment` with `issueId: <issue-id>`, `body`.
107	
108	**Output:** confirmation the comment was posted.
109	
110	## set_status
111	
112	**Inputs:** issue id, target status name.
113	
114	**Procedure:**
115	
116	1. Resolve `status_name` to a state id via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issue_statuses` scoped to the issue's team. Do this lookup **fresh each call** — do not cache status ids across a run (workflow states can differ by team, and a cached id from one team's workflow is not portable to another).
117	2. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue` with `id: <issue-id>`, `stateId: <resolved-id>`.
118	
119	**Output:** confirmation the status changed.
120	
121	## attach_link
122	
123	**Inputs:** issue id, URL.
124	
125	**Procedure:**
126	
127	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__create_attachment` with `issueId: <issue-id>`, `url`. Always an unconditional, explicit attachment call — this fragment makes no claim that Linear auto-links a PR from body text (that would depend on a workspace-level Linear↔GitHub integration this fragment cannot assume).
128	
129	**Output:** confirmation the link is attached (the tool's response).
130	
131	## list_by_status
132	
133	**Inputs:** target status name; team scope (and project scope when **Linear Project** is configured).
134	
135	**Procedure:**
136	
137	1. Resolve `status_name` to a state id via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issue_statuses` scoped to the resolved team. Do this lookup **fresh each call** — do not cache status ids across a run (workflow states differ by team; a cached id is not portable). Same discipline as `set_status`.
138	2. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues` filtered to that `stateId`, scoped by the resolved `teamId` (and `projectId` when **Linear Project** is configured).
139	
140	**Output:** the matching issues (id + title + status), or an empty list when none match — a read never writes. On tool error, the caller applies the contract's mid-run-failure degradation rule.
141	
142	## list_milestones
143	
144	**Inputs:** project scope (the resolved `projectId`; Linear milestones are a project-scoped concept).
145	
146	**Procedure:**
147	
148	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_milestones` scoped to the resolved `projectId` (from "Team/project id resolution" above). When **Linear Project** is the literal `none` (no project configured), there is no project to enumerate milestones for — return an **empty list**, not an error.
149	
150	**Output:** the project's milestones (id + name + target date where present), or an empty list — a read never writes. On tool error, the caller applies the contract's mid-run-failure degradation rule.
151	
152	## list_cycles
153	
154	**Inputs:** team scope (the resolved `teamId`; Linear cycles are a team-scoped concept).
155	
156	**Procedure:**
157	
158	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_cycles` filtered to the resolved `teamId` (from "Team/project id resolution" above).
159	
160	**Output:** the team's cycles (id + name + start/end where present), or an empty list — a read never writes. On tool error, the caller applies the contract's mid-run-failure degradation rule.
161	
162	## list_blockers
163	
164	**Inputs:** task (issue) id — the blocked task whose blocking predecessors to read.
165	
166	**Procedure:**
167	
168	1. Call `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue` with `id: <issue-id>` and `includeRelations: true` — Linear returns the issue's relations, including the `blockedBy` set (the issues that block this one).
169	2. Read the `blockedBy` relation set from the response; each entry's identifier (`<LETTERS>-<NUMBER>`) is a blocking predecessor.
170	
171	**Output:** the set of blocking issue identifiers, or an **empty set** when the issue has no `blockedBy` relations — a read never writes, and no-blockers is not an error. On tool error, the caller applies the contract's mid-run-failure degradation rule.

# /wf:spec — interface declaration

The machine-readable, externally-bindable surface of `spec`. A resolver reads
this file for the skill's declared slots and settings — **never** the SKILL.md
body. Everything in the body outside the declared slot markers is freely
rewordable implementation; the five sections below are the stable, contracted
surface (invocation shape, terminal block, slots + merge policies, settings
keys, safety rules).

## Invocation

`/wf:spec [<id>] [--type feat|fix|chore|refactor|migration|docs|hotfix] [--complexity S|M|L]`

## Terminal block

`SPEC — Complete`

## Slots

| slot (skill.point) | merge policy | purpose                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| spec.publish       | replace      | publish the written spec artifact to a registered tracker after `01_spec.md` is written (Phase 3); the inline default publishes nothing beyond the local task folder |
| spec.questions     | replace      | mirror the phase's open questions to a registered tracker before the interactive question prompt (Phase 2); the inline default mirrors nothing                       |

## Settings

_(none)_

## Safety rules

**Allowed:** read the task folder and its artifacts; obtain config via the
`wf-resolver` `resolve_config({ workspaceRoot, ... })` query; fetch requirements
and apply the single Phase 0 step-3 `update` backfill through the active tracker

# spec.publish — publish the written spec to the tracker (slot fill)


Before following any resolver MCP call in this document, run `pwd -P` and use the returned absolute current Agent/session workspace directory as `workspaceRoot`. In a linked-worktree Agent, that cwd is the Agent's own worktree; never inherit a parent root. Pass it explicitly on every call. Omitting `workspaceRoot` is a hard schema error; resolver MCP calls have no default or fallback root.

The `linear` capability's fill for the `spec.publish` slot (`replace` policy). `spec` reaches
this point **after** Phase 3 has written `01_spec.md` and updated the per-task index, and
**before** the phase's Final Output block. Because this is a `replace` fill it **supersedes**
`spec`'s inline default (the no-op "publish nothing beyond the local task folder") wholesale,
and `spec` follows this prose in its own context.

**Role framing.** This fill mirrors the just-written spec artifact onto the tracker so a
tracker-bound reader can read the spec without the local task folder. It performs exactly
**one publish per spec artifact** — no second write, no duplicate. It is a **distinct write**
from the Phase 0 step-3 "Dev" backfill `update` (which patches a different work item's
*description* field); the two never collide and neither substitutes for the other. On any
failure it warns once and returns quietly — `spec` still emits its Final Output block; a
tracker failure never blocks the phase.

**Tracker access.** Every operation below is a `tracker`-surface operation reached by resolving
the active tracker provider (`resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "tracker" })`) and
obtaining each op's body via `resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` (`class: fragment`) — bind
only the abstract contract ops named here, never a concrete host tool string. The ops this fill
uses: `create_umbrella` (create-or-reuse the umbrella), `create_child` (publish the spec
sub-issue), `set_status` (mark it done). All three already exist in the tracker contract; this
fill requires no new op.

**Configured guard.** If the resolved tracker state is `unconfigured` (no tracker registered) or
`unrecoverable`, publish nothing and return quietly — the inline no-op default's outcome —
applying the contract's degradation discipline (silent on unconfigured; one hedged warn-once on
unrecoverable naming the candidate pack). Continue only when a tracker is configured.

---

## Step 1 — Ensure the umbrella exists (create or reuse)

Resolve the umbrella work item for this task's parent context, using `create_umbrella`'s
recorded-id idempotency guard:

- If the local task artifact already records an umbrella id (a `**Umbrella:** <id>` metadata
  line written by a prior fire on this task — this fill's own or the `spec.questions` fill's),
  **reuse it** — read the line back first and never re-create.
- Otherwise invoke `create_umbrella(<task title>, <task description>)` and record the returned
  id as a `**Umbrella:** <id>` metadata line in the task's local artifact, so a later fire (or
  the `spec.questions` fill) reuses it rather than double-creating.

## Step 2 — Publish the spec as a done sub-issue (one write per artifact)

Read the full markdown of the just-written `01_spec.md` from the task folder. Then:

- Invoke `create_child(<umbrella id>, "Spec: <task title>", <full 01_spec.md markdown>)` to
  publish the spec as a sub-issue of the umbrella. The `Spec:` title prefix labels it as a spec
  artifact. Guard with the same recorded-id idempotency check: if a `**Spec issue:** <id>` line
  already exists for this artifact, reuse it (patch its body via the contract's `update` when
  the spec was rewritten) rather than creating a duplicate. Record the returned id as
  `**Spec issue:** <id>`.
- Invoke `set_status(<spec sub-issue id>, "Done")` to mark the published spec Done — it records a
  completed artifact, not open work.

## Step 3 — Return

The spec artifact is now mirrored on the tracker as a Done `Spec:` sub-issue of the umbrella.
Return quietly so `spec` proceeds to its Final Output block. Carry a one-line note into the
phase's report (e.g. `Published: Spec sub-issue <id> (Done) under umbrella <id>`).

# spec.questions — mirror open questions to the tracker parent (slot fill)


Before following any resolver MCP call in this document, run `pwd -P` and use the returned absolute current Agent/session workspace directory as `workspaceRoot`. In a linked-worktree Agent, that cwd is the Agent's own worktree; never inherit a parent root. Pass it explicitly on every call. Omitting `workspaceRoot` is a hard schema error; resolver MCP calls have no default or fallback root.

The `linear` capability's fill for the `spec.questions` slot (`replace` policy). `spec` reaches
this point in Phase 2 **after** the open questions are identified and **before** the interactive
`AskUserQuestion` prompt. Because this is a `replace` fill it **supersedes** `spec`'s inline
default (the no-op "mirror nothing") wholesale, and `spec` follows this prose in its own
context, then continues to the interactive prompt.

**Role framing.** This fill posts the phase's open questions as a **single** parent comment on
the umbrella, so a tracker-bound reader sees the questions before they are resolved
interactively. It posts **one** comment per fire — never one-per-question, never a duplicate. It
never blocks: on any failure it warns once and returns quietly, and `spec` still runs its
interactive prompt. It never posts the questions onto the task's own child item — only the
umbrella parent.

**Tracker access.** As with the `spec.publish` fill, resolve the active tracker provider
(`resolve_provider({ workspaceRoot, surface: "tracker" })`) and obtain each op's body via
`resolve_content({ workspaceRoot, ... })` (`class: fragment`) — bind only the abstract contract
ops: `create_umbrella` (create-or-reuse the umbrella, sharing the recorded-id idempotency guard
so it never double-creates) and `post_comment` (post the questions to the umbrella). Both already
exist; this fill requires no new op.

**Configured guard.** If the tracker is `unconfigured`/`unrecoverable`, or there are **no open
questions** this fire, mirror nothing and return quietly (the inline no-op default's outcome),
then continue to the interactive prompt.

---

## Step 1 — Ensure the umbrella exists (shared idempotency guard)

Resolve the umbrella exactly as the `spec.publish` fill does: reuse the recorded
`**Umbrella:** <id>` metadata line when present; otherwise `create_umbrella(<task title>, <task
description>)` and record the id. The two fills share this one guard so a single umbrella exists
per task, never one per slot.

## Step 2 — Post the open questions as one parent comment

Compose the identified open questions into a single markdown body (a short titled list). Invoke
`post_comment(<umbrella id>, <questions markdown>)` **exactly once**. Guard against a duplicate:
if a `**Questions comment:** posted` marker already exists for this fire, skip the post. Record
`**Questions comment:** posted`.

## Step 3 — Return

The open questions are mirrored as one parent comment on the umbrella. Return quietly so `spec`
proceeds to its interactive `AskUserQuestion` prompt — the local resolution flow is unchanged.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# skill-slot-marker-lint.sh — CI lint for the skill interface slot-marker syntax
3	# (WF-326, charter C014 / WF-322 SUB-3).
4	#
5	# WF-326 formalized the skill interface as a contracted shape: a skill's
6	# externally-bindable surface (invocation shape, terminal block, declared slots
7	# with merge policies, declared settings keys, safety rules) is declared in a
8	# machine-readable sidecar — `skills/<name>/interface.md` — so a resolver can
9	# learn a skill's slots/settings WITHOUT reading its SKILL.md body (the
10	# resolver's `resolve_content` refuses skill-body reads). A slot is placed in a
11	# SKILL.md body with a grep-validatable marker pair. This lint keeps the body
12	# markers and the interface declaration honest against each other.
13	#
14	# Full syntax + rationale: capability-registry.contract.md
15	# ("The skill interface declaration + slot markers"); the runtime-followed rules
16	# are in capability-registry.ops.md (same heading).
17	#
18	# --- The marker syntax (what a well-formed marker is) ---
19	# A slot occupies a body region delimited by an HTML-comment pair, each marker
20	# ALONE on its line (surrounding whitespace tolerated), naming the same slot id:
21	#
22	#     <!-- wf:slot <skill>.<point> -->
23	#     ...the inline-default region (executed verbatim when the slot is unfilled)...
24	#     <!-- wf:slot-end <skill>.<point> -->
25	#
26	# The slot id is a `skill.point` token (WF-323 vocabulary): two segments joined
27	# by a single dot, each segment lowercase letters / digits / hyphens; the first
28	# segment (`<skill>`) MUST equal the skill's folder name.
29	#
30	# --- The declaration (interface.md ## Slots) ---
31	# `skills/<name>/interface.md` declares each slot in a `## Slots` table whose
32	# first column is the `skill.point` id and second column the merge policy
33	# (`replace` | `append`, the WF-323 policies). The lint reads ONLY this table
34	# for the declared set — never the SKILL.md body prose.
35	#
36	# --- What the lint flags (each with file:line and the defect) ---
37	#   D1 malformed declaration — a `## Slots` row whose id is not a well-formed
38	#      `skill.point`, whose first segment is not the folder name, or whose merge
39	#      policy is absent / not `replace`|`append`.
40	#   D2 malformed marker — a `<!-- wf:slot… -->` comment that is not EXACTLY an
41	#      opening or closing marker with a well-formed id on its own line.
42	#   D3 undeclared marker — a well-formed marker whose slot id has no matching
43	#      `## Slots` declaration in the same skill's interface.md.
44	#   D4 unbalanced marker — an opening marker with no matching close (or a close
45	#      with no open), or a duplicate opening marker for one slot.
46	#   D5 declared-but-unmarked — a declared slot with no opening marker in SKILL.md.
47	#
48	# --- Why it is inert on the existing tree ---
49	# A skill with no `## Slots` declarations and no `<!-- wf:slot… -->` markers
50	# produces zero declared ids and zero marker hits — every loop body is empty, so
51	# it emits nothing. The whole current skill tree (which declares no slots yet)
52	# passes unchanged.
53	#
54	# --- Scope (path) ---
55	# Scanned:  plugins/*/skills/*/ — every skill folder across ALL packs (a folder
56	#           counts as a skill only if it holds a SKILL.md).
57	# NOT scanned: plugins/*/skills/_contracts/** — the frozen contract layer, THIS
58	#           script, and slot-marker-fixtures/ (the deliberate pass/fail cases the
59	#           --selftest exercises). `_contracts/` itself holds no SKILL.md, and the
60	#           fixtures sit two levels deeper than the `plugins/*/skills/*/` glob, so
61	#           the real-tree scan never reaches them.
62	#
63	# Requires GNU/PCRE grep (`grep -P`; present on the Linux CI runner and Git Bash).
64	# Exit 0 = clean; exit 1 = a defect was found; exit 2 = grep/PCRE error (never a
65	# silent pass). With `--selftest`: runs the linter over slot-marker-fixtures/ and
66	# asserts each planted pass/fail case behaves as specified — proving the linter
67	# discriminates before it is trusted on the real tree.
68	#
69	# Wired into CI by registry-fixtures/run.sh (the established guard chain that
70	# .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes) — this lint is NOT auto-discovered.
71	#
72	# Model: claude-opus-4-8
73	set -u
74	
75	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../.." && pwd)"   # -> repo root
76	FIXROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/slot-marker-fixtures"
77	
78	# A well-formed skill.point: two dot-joined segments, each [a-z0-9-]+.
79	idre='[a-z0-9-]+\.[a-z0-9-]+'
80	
81	# trim leading/trailing whitespace.
82	trim() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//'; }
83	
84	# in_set <needle> <space-separated-haystack> — 0 if present.
85	in_set() { case " $2 " in *" $1 "*) return 0;; *) return 1;; esac; }
86	
87	# lint_skill_dir <dir> — lints one skill folder, echoing one line per defect
88	# (nothing when clean). Reads interface.md for the declared slots and SKILL.md
89	# only for its own markers.
90	lint_skill_dir() {
91	  local dir="${1%/}"
92	  local skill body iface
93	  skill="$(basename "$dir")"
94	  body="$dir/SKILL.md"
95	  iface="$dir/interface.md"
96	  [ -f "$body" ] || return 0    # not a skill folder — inert
97	
98	  # --- 1. declared slots from interface.md's ## Slots table -----------------
99	  local declared="" decl_lines="" inslots=0 lineno=0 line c1 c2 rest seg1
100	  if [ -f "$iface" ]; then
101	    while IFS= read -r line; do
102	      lineno=$((lineno + 1))
103	      case "$line" in
104	        '## Slots'*) inslots=1; continue;;
105	        '## '*)      inslots=0;;
106	      esac
107	      [ "$inslots" -eq 1 ] || continue
108	      case "$line" in '|'*) ;; *) continue;; esac   # a table row only
109	      c1="${line#|}"; c1="${c1%%|*}"
110	      rest="${line#|}"; rest="${rest#*|}"; c2="${rest%%|*}"
111	      c1="$(trim "$c1")"; c2="$(trim "$c2")"
112	      # Skip the header row and the |---| separator: a declared id has no space
113	      # or paren, contains an alnum, and is not a pure-dash rule.
114	      case "$c1" in ''|*' '*|*'('*) continue;; esac
115	      case "$c1" in *[a-z0-9]*) ;; *) continue;; esac
116	      if ! printf '%s' "$c1" | grep -Pq "^${idre}\$"; then
117	        echo "$iface:$lineno: malformed slot declaration '$c1' — a slot id must be <skill>.<point> (each segment lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, exactly one dot)."
118	        continue
119	      fi
120	      seg1="${c1%%.*}"
121	      if [ "$seg1" != "$skill" ]; then
122	        echo "$iface:$lineno: slot id '$c1' names skill '$seg1' but is declared under skill '$skill' — the id's first segment must match the skill folder name."
123	        continue
124	      fi
125	      case "$c2" in
126	        replace|append) ;;
127	        '') echo "$iface:$lineno: slot '$c1' declares no merge policy (expected 'replace' or 'append')."; continue;;
128	        *)  echo "$iface:$lineno: slot '$c1' has unknown merge policy '$c2' (expected 'replace' or 'append')."; continue;;
129	      esac
130	      declared="$declared $c1"
131	      decl_lines="$decl_lines $c1:$lineno"
132	    done < "$iface"
133	  fi
134	
135	  # --- 2. scan SKILL.md markers --------------------------------------------
136	  local opens="" closes="" hit lno content trimmed id rc
137	  local open_re="^<!-- wf:slot (${idre}) -->\$"
138	  local close_re="^<!-- wf:slot-end (${idre}) -->\$"
139	  local grep_out
140	  grep_out="$(grep -Pn '<!--\s*wf:slot' "$body")"
141	  rc=$?
142	  if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then
143	    echo "$body: ERROR — grep failed (rc=$rc); this lint requires PCRE grep (grep -P)."
144	    return 2
145	  fi
146	  while IFS= read -r hit; do
147	    [ -n "$hit" ] || continue
148	    lno="${hit%%:*}"; content="${hit#*:}"
149	    trimmed="$(trim "$content")"
150	    if [[ "$trimmed" =~ $open_re ]]; then
151	      id="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
152	      if in_set "$id" "$opens"; then
153	        echo "$body:$lno: duplicate opening marker for slot '$id'."
154	      fi
155	      opens="$opens $id"
156	      if ! in_set "$id" "$declared"; then
157	        echo "$body:$lno: slot marker '$id' is not declared in $skill/interface.md (## Slots)."
158	      fi
159	    elif [[ "$trimmed" =~ $close_re ]]; then
160	      id="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
161	      closes="$closes $id"
162	    else
163	      echo "$body:$lno: malformed slot marker: '$trimmed' — expected exactly '<!-- wf:slot <skill.point> -->' or '<!-- wf:slot-end <skill.point> -->' alone on its line."
164	    fi
165	  done <<EOF
166	$grep_out
167	EOF
168	
169	  # --- 3. balance + declared-has-marker ------------------------------------
170	  local pair dl
171	  for id in $opens; do
172	    in_set "$id" "$closes" || echo "$body: opening marker for slot '$id' has no matching '<!-- wf:slot-end $id -->' close."
173	  done
174	  for id in $closes; do
175	    in_set "$id" "$opens" || echo "$body: closing marker for slot '$id' has no matching opening marker."
176	  done
177	  for pair in $decl_lines; do
178	    id="${pair%%:*}"; dl="${pair##*:}"
179	    in_set "$id" "$opens" || echo "$iface:$dl: declared slot '$id' has no '<!-- wf:slot $id -->' marker in $skill/SKILL.md."
180	  done
181	  return 0
182	}
183	
184	# --- --selftest: drive the fixtures --------------------------------------------
185	if [ "${1:-}" = "--selftest" ]; then
186	  st_fails=0
187	  # check_pass <fixture>
188	  check_pass() {
189	    local out; out="$(lint_skill_dir "$FIXROOT/$1")"
190	    if [ -n "$out" ]; then
191	      echo "selftest FAIL: $1 — expected CLEAN, got defects:"; echo "$out"
192	      st_fails=$((st_fails + 1))
193	    else
194	      echo "selftest ok (pass): $1"
195	    fi
196	  }
197	  # check_fail <fixture> <required-substring>...
198	  check_fail() {
199	    local fx="$1"; shift
200	    local out; out="$(lint_skill_dir "$FIXROOT/$fx")"
201	    if [ -z "$out" ]; then
202	      echo "selftest FAIL: $fx — expected a defect, got CLEAN."
203	      st_fails=$((st_fails + 1)); return
204	    fi
205	    local s ok=1
206	    for s in "$@"; do
207	      case "$out" in *"$s"*) ;; *) ok=0; echo "selftest FAIL: $fx — output missing '$s'. Got:"; echo "$out";; esac
208	    done
209	    [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && echo "selftest ok (fail): $fx"
210	  }
211	
212	  # Passing cases — the linter must stay silent.
213	  check_pass slotfree
214	  check_pass wellformed-replace
215	  check_pass wellformed-append
216	
217	  # Failing cases — one defect class each, defect must name file:line + reason.
218	  check_fail malformed-marker    "SKILL.md:" "malformed slot marker"
219	  check_fail undeclared-marker   "SKILL.md:" "is not declared"
220	  check_fail missing-marker      "interface.md:" "has no" "marker"
221	  check_fail unbalanced          "no matching"
222	  check_fail bad-declaration     "interface.md:" "malformed slot declaration"
223	
224	  echo ""
225	  if [ "$st_fails" -ne 0 ]; then
226	    echo "OUT-SLOT selftest: FAIL — $st_fails fixture case(s) misbehaved."
227	    exit 1
228	  fi
229	  echo "OUT-SLOT selftest: PASS — every planted pass/fail fixture behaves as specified."
230	  exit 0
231	fi
232	
233	# --- Default: scan the real skill tree ----------------------------------------
234	hits=""
235	rc_any=0
236	for dir in "$ROOT"/plugins/*/skills/*/; do
237	  [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
238	  out="$(lint_skill_dir "$dir")"; rc=$?
239	  if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then rc_any=2; fi
240	  [ -n "$out" ] && hits="$hits$out"$'\n'
241	done
242	
243	if [ "$rc_any" -ge 2 ]; then
244	  echo "OUT-SLOT: ERROR — grep failed (requires PCRE grep -P)."
245	  exit 2
246	fi
247	if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
248	  echo "OUT-SLOT: FAIL — skill slot markers / interface declarations are inconsistent:"
249	  printf '%s' "$hits"
250	  exit 1
251	fi
252	echo "OUT-SLOT: PASS — every skill's slot markers agree with its interface declaration (inert where none are declared)."
253	exit 0
